items.title: UK to pay France £660M in new deal to curb Channel crossings

featured_image.name: UK Links France's Border Plan Funding to Performance in New ...

items.description:
The United Kingdom has agreed to pay France roughly £660 million over three years in a new deal to curb illegal small boat crossings of the English Channel, with Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood set to formally sign the agreement on Thursday, according to the Guardian.[1]

The deal, which will run until March 2029, comes after weeks of fraught negotiations that saw the previous £478 million arrangement expire on March 31 and required a £16.2 million emergency two-month extension to keep patrols running while talks continued.[2][3]

items.title: Zelensky distances himself from 'Donnyland' Donbas proposal, pushes to restart talks

featured_image.name: Ukraine proposes creating 'Donnyland' to satisfy Trump - Yahoo

items.description:
President Volodymyr Zelensky pushed back on Wednesday against a reported proposal by Ukrainian negotiators to rename a contested strip of the Donbas region "Donnyland" — a portmanteau of Donetsk, Donald, and Disneyland — as a diplomatic gesture aimed at winning the favor of U.S. President Donald Trump.

"The main thing is that Donetsk Oblast and Luhansk Oblast remain Ukraine — as long as it's not 'Putinland.' That is the most important thing," Zelensky told reporters on April 22, according to the Kyiv Independent. He added that in negotiations he uses "no other terms than Donetsk Oblast, Luhansk Oblast, our Donbas, and the territory of Ukraine."[1]

items.title: Pentagon says clearing Hormuz mines could take 6 months

items.description: The Pentagon has informed Congress that fully clearing Iranian sea mines from the Strait of Hormuz could take up to six months, and that the operation is unlikely to be completed before the war with Iran ends, according to a Washington Post exclusive report published Wednesday. The assessment, delivered during a classified briefing for members of the House Armed Services Committee on April 21, paints a far grimmer picture of the mine threat than the optimistic tone struck by President Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in recent weeks.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Iran seizes two ships, fires on third in Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Iran fires on, seizes two container ships near Strait of Hormuz

items.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps opened fire on three commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, seizing two and leaving a third stranded along the Iranian coast, in a sharp escalation that came just hours after President Trump announced he was indefinitely extending a ceasefire with Tehran.

The IRGC captured the Panama-flagged MSC Francesca and the Liberia-flagged Epaminondas, both container ships, and directed them to Iranian waters, according to a statement carried by AFP. A third vessel, the Greek-owned Euphoria, was also targeted and is now stranded off the Iranian coast, according to semiofficial Iranian news agency Fars. The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency reported that the first ship was "assaulted by a gunboat" from the IRGC at approximately 7:55 a.m. local time.[1][2][3][4][5]

The IRGC claimed the vessels "allegedly operated without authorization, repeatedly violated regulations, manipulated navigational aid systems and sought to covertly exit the Strait of Hormuz, endangering maritime security". The statement added that "disruption of order and safety in the Strait of Hormuz is our red line".[6][1]

items.description: European Union ambassadors are expected to approve a long-delayed €90 billion loan to Ukraine on Wednesday, removing the last financial roadblock that had threatened to leave Kyiv without funding as it fights off Russia's invasion. The vote at the Committee of Permanent Representatives in Brussels comes just ten days after Viktor Orban's historic election defeat in Hungary ended his 16-year grip on power and, with it, Budapest's blockade of the aid package.
